title.narrative: Save the Children Afghanistan, Child protection 2016-2021

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention is to strengthened child protection prevention initiatives and quality access to child protection response services and reduce instances of violence, exploitation and neglect of children. Specifically, the project seeks to strengthen child protection systems at the national, provincial, district and community level to protect children at risk of abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect.
Following are the results to be achieved at outcome level:
Result 1: Strengthened community and formal government child protection systems (referring to before the political transition in August 2021) improve access to and utilization of preventive and response services.
Result 2: Violence against children is no longer tolerated in schools and at homes.
Result 3: Children involved in or at risk of entering harmful work can access adequate support and protection that reduce their risk and improves their own and their families' livelihood opportunities as a way out of hazardous work.
Result 4: Local Civil Society organizations (CSOs) demonstrate enhanced organizational operation capacity and more specific capacity in child rights and protection programming.
Result 5: Community institutions, including those led by children and youth, are better able to respond to disasters affecting them.
Result 6: Boys and girls are protected from the direct impact of conflict through the prevention and response to recruitment and use by armed forces or armed groups and indirect impact through awareness-raising and community-based risk reduction activities (Nangarhar province).

Den föreslagna insatsen är en fortsättning av Rädda Barnens/Save the Childrens projekt för barns rätt till trygghet och skydd i Afghanistan (som pågått 2013 - 2015). Den nya insatsen är planerad att pågå 2016-2019 i sex provinser. Fem av provinserna är samma som i projektets första fas: Nangarhar, Sa-re-Pul, Jawzjan, Balkh och Kabul. En sjätte provins, Faryad, har tillkommit i och med att en humanitär komponent tagits över från Rädda Barnens humanitära barnrättsprogram i Afghanistan. Det är ett led i Sidas ansträngningar att öka arbetet med transition, dvs. överbryggning mellan humanitärt stöd och utvecklingsstöd. Möjligheten fanns i och med att Rädda Barnen varit verksamt med båda stödformerna i Afghanistan. Nu ges det humanitära arbetet möjlighet att arbeta mer med långsiktigt stöd i den svåra utdragna konflikten. Den humanitära komponenten och transitionen ska utvärderas under år två.
Det övergripande målet för insatsen är att stärka barns rätt till trygghet och skydd, på en nationell, provinsiell, distrikt- och samhällsnivå i Afghanistan och att minska förekomsten av exploatering, försummelse, våld och övergrepp mot barn. Insatsen är ett projekt.
Projektet kommer att inledas med en fem månader lång s.k. "Inception phase", en inledningsfas med start i januari 2016 och rapporteras i en slutrapport i juni 2016.
Konfliktkänslighet är A och O givet den svåra situationen för mänskliga rättigheter i Afghanistan. Den inledande beredningen föreslog en projektperiod på tre år. Huvudberedningen och detta beslut föreslår en projektperiod på fyra år, då en fyraårig insats har också bättre förutsättningar att mäta resultat. Resultatstrategin för utvecklingssamarbetet med Afghanistan 2015 - 2019 ger också utrymme för det. Insatsens totala budget ligger i samband med ansökan på 49 700 000 SEK.
Insatsen har förlängts till 2020 och är därmed på totalt 62 700 000 SEK.
Sida är den enda givaren.

The proposed intervention will build and expand on the previous project phase 2013-2015. The project will be implemented during the four-year period from 2016 to 2019 in six provinces. Five of the provinces are the same as in the previous project phase: Nangarhar, Sa-re-Pul, Jawzjan, Balkh and Kabul. An additional sixth province is added; Faryab as an additional humanitarian component was included in the project as transition from Save the Children's humanitarian work in Afghanistan. This is a part of Sida’s efforts to link humanitarian assistance with development aid.
The overall objective of this program is strengthened child protection prevention initiatives and quality access to child protection response services reduce instances of violence, exploitation and neglect of children. Specifically, the program seeks to strengthen child protection systems at the national, provincial, district and community level to protect children at risk of abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect.
The project will begin with a five-month "Inception Phase starting in January 2016 and be reported in an inception report in June 2016.
Conflict sensitivity is key, given the difficult situation of human rights in Afghanistan. The initial assessment suggested a project period of three years. The appraisal, and this decision is proposing a project period of four years as a four-year effort is better placed to measure results. The Results Strategy for Development Cooperation with Afghanistan 2015 - 2019 also allows for this. The total budget as of the application was 49.7 million SEK.
The contribution has been extended until 2020 and the total budget is 62.7 million SEK.
Sida is the only donor.

During 2020 there were serious security challenges and political instability and the COVID-19 pandemic made the operating environment even more challenging. Despite these changes the major achievements of selective activities are as follows:
Result area 1: Strengthened community and formal government child protection systems and access to preventative and response services (System strengthening refers before the political transition in August 2021). Community based child protection networks members (CBCPN) in five provinces were trained in safe identification and referrals. The training resulted in a heightened capacity to effectively respond to cases of abuse and to direct the ones affected to the right services. This made the number of children that were identified and helped during 2020 higher than in 2019. Which also means that the network members are more trusted. Since network members were not allowed to attend community gatherings because of the pandemic, they instead did safe door-to-door activities with awareness messages. During 2020 170 networks added a focus on child marriage, as the risk became more evident during the pandemic. The database of service providers were also updated so that children could receive timely support and village leaders learned strategies on how to talk to parents to encourage them to send their children (girls) to school. Additionally, there was an orientation with 1.700 participants on Gender from an Islamic Perspective (training manual), this orientation have led to significant changes in behaviour of male family members according to reportings from female network members.
Result area 2: Violence against children not tolerated in school or at home. The Child-led Participatory Situational Analysis is a core activity to ensure meaningful child participation in program design and adaptation. There is also a feedback mechanism where children can share their views and feedback on the program. School Student Councils were established which made it possible to monitor child right violations both at schools and at home. Additionally, teacher to teacher trainings took place which was reported to have been effective. In total 740 teachers in five provinces were trained on the negative effects of Physical Humiliating Punishment and as a result there have been reports on less violence in schools. To address gender inequalities, a contextual training on the fatherhood manual with 480 fathers were held. The interest of fathers to attend had increased exponentially since fathers from the previous years and reports on the results have been coming in from females of the households that the role of the husband and father had changed significantly after the training. There were also 800 children that were educated on their rights and protection and to say no to violations to support violence-free schools.
Result area 3: Children at risk of entering harmful work have access to support and protection. The project team (in collaboration with CBCPNs and CGs) conducted a vulnerability mapping exercise in six provinces to identify the most vulnerable children. Communities were mobilised to contribute to the program and to facilitate the reintegration of children into state schools. The number of children removed from the streets in six provinces increased in comparison to the last year and 901 children were enrolled in community children centers where they received psychological support, case management and educated in childs rights. A market assessment took place to measure the market demand on the income generating activities. In 2019, 35% of business were female led where as in 2020, 44% were female led. This is a positive increase of women into the economic life. A training of 577 parents and caregivers of working children took place, this lead to a positive change in the action and attitudes of the adults that partook in the training. Additionally, employers were engaged in a program to prevent child abuse and exploitation. As a result, 182 male employers were trained on childs rights.
Result area 4: Local civil society organisations have more operational capacity and specifically in child protection programming. The civil society organisations (CSO) enjoys a high level of trust in their communities, in 2020 the CSOs took on an advisory role to support program implementation and design, providing expertise on the local contexts. This helped to improve the programs. CSOs had initiatives and campaigns regarding the child protection issue, their involvement in this was also helpful to address existing child protection issues in the communities. For example, 53 police officers were trained on child rights during 2020 and informative sessions on COVID-19 were held with 400 children. during 2020 Haya, a female led CSO supported a female campaign on awareness-raising of womens rights and child marriage in conservative communities.
Result area 5: Community institutions are better equipped to respond to disasters affecting them. In 2020, 10 staff members were educated in the Psychological First Aid (PFA), because of this the project could ensure that each targeted province has a PFA focal point. This also helped communities to receive on-time support during the pandemic. Especially concerning children that were abused and had a violent home or workplace. During 2020, the work to scale up the inclusion of children with disabilities begun. Training and awareness events on rights of children with disabilities took place which was shown to change the perception that people have on children with disabilities. However, still much work has to be done, especially in schools.
Result area 6: Children are more protected from recruitment to armed forces and groups through awareness raising measures. During 2020, six child friendly spaces (CFS) focusing on internally displaced persons (IDP) were established. Totally 320 children participated in the CFS and were referred to service providers. The children also received health education, PFA and awareness session on the prevention of COVID-19. Since most of the children did not have a National Identity Card due to displacement, many got help to access the cards so that they could get enrolled in school. There were also a mass awareness-raising campaign during 2020 on child rights and protection and child/early or forced marriage and recruitment of children into armed forces or groups. The participation of religious leaders in the dialogue with the family has been key for success in convincing families not to follow through with the child marriages.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
